title: 6.30.3 Lab: Kings, and the win
description: Pieces are crowned on the far row and kings move both ways; crowning ends a chain; a player with no move left loses, and R plays again.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: This is your game from 6.29.3: steps, jumps and chains. A piece that reaches the far side just stops there, and the game never ends.

steps.title: Kings are letters too
steps.instructions: Change `colorOf` to `function colorOf(p) { return p.toLowerCase(); }` and add `function isKing(p) { return p === 'R' || p === 'B'; }` below it. In `drawPieces`, after the two circles, `if (isKing(p)) text('K', x - 6, y + 7, 20, 'gold');`. Run: nothing looks different yet, because no piece is a king.
hints: `''.toLowerCase()` is `''`, so an empty square still has no colour.

steps.title: Crown on the far row
steps.instructions: Write `crown(r, c)` from the reading, below `doMove`. In `doMove`, after the jumped piece is taken, add `const crowned = crown(tr, tc);` and change the chain test to `if (kind === 'jump' && !crowned && canJumpFrom(tr, tc))`. Run and get a red piece to row 0: it shows a gold K.
hints: Crown after the piece has moved: `crown` reads the letter at the landing square.
A crowned piece stops its chain: `!crowned` makes the turn pass.

steps.title: A king moves back
steps.instructions: In `moveKind`, change `if (!ahead) return '';` to `if (!ahead && !isKing(p)) return '';`. Run: a king steps and jumps backward; a plain piece still cannot.

steps.title: No move, no game
steps.instructions: Add `let winner = '';` at the top and `winner = '';` in `newGame()`. Write `hasAnyMove()` from the reading. At the end of `doMove`, after the turn passes: `if (!hasAnyMove()) { winner = turn === 'r' ? 'b' : 'r'; message = nameOf(winner) + ' wins! Press R to play again'; }`. In `draw()`, clicks only count while nobody has won, `if (mouse.presses() && winner === '') clickAt(mouse.x, mouse.y);`, and `if (kb.presses('r') && winner !== '') newGame();`.
hints: Ask after the turn has passed: the player who has no move is the one whose turn it now is.
To test it fast, change `r < 3` in `makeBoard` to `r < 1` so black starts with only 4 pieces. Put it back after.

requirements.title: Crowned on the far row
requirements.description: A red piece on row 0 becomes 'R', and a black piece on the last row becomes 'B'. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)

requirements.title: A king can move back
requirements.description: The forward-only rule does not hold a king back: a king may move both ways. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)

requirements.title: A check for no moves
requirements.description: A function asks about every square of the board whether the player whose turn it is has any move left. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)
requirements.hint: function hasAnyMove() { for (...) { for (...) { if (moveKind(...) !== '') return true; } } return false; }

requirements.title: A winner, and R to play again
requirements.description: Once someone has won, R starts a new game. Help: 6.30.1 (Reading: Kings, and a player with no move)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Kings, and the win". The task: crown a piece that lands on its far row ('r' on row 0 becomes 'R', 'b' on the last row becomes 'B'); make colorOf use toLowerCase so a king still belongs to its colour; let a king move backward; end a chain when a piece is crowned; after the turn passes, a player with no legal move (hasAnyMove asks moveKind about every square) loses, clicks stop, and R starts a new game. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Crowned

rubric.title: No move

rubric.title: Play again
rubric.description: Someone wins, and R starts again.
